target_customer: Consumers and families with smart speakers, later smart TVs, who pay by subscription or in-skill purchase for voice-controlled games
problem: Voice assistants and smart TVs had little engaging native entertainment, so living rooms lacked group games that people could play out loud together.
business_model: Consumer subscription and in-app purchases for voice games, plus licensed game show and kids brand partnerships
product_category: Voice-controlled games and entertainment for smart speakers and TVs

founders.name: Max Child
founders.background_notes: Named as founder and CEO on the YC page. Education and prior employers not found in sources opened.

founders.name: James Wilsterman
founders.background_notes: Named as founder and CTO on the YC page. Education and prior employers not found in sources opened.

competitors.name: Earplay
competitors.what: Interactive audio-only storytelling skill for Alexa, launched August 2016
competitors.traction_then: Named Developer of the Year at the 2018 Alexa Conference Awards per its own site

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice games on Alexa meant speech recognition handled by Amazon, so the hard parts were game design, content pipelines and retention. Later TV and AI work raised the bar but not at founding.

defensibility.rationale: Skills on a shared platform were easy to copy. Early lead came from chart position and content cadence (Song Quiz and Yes Sire held the top two Alexa spots in 2018). Later licenses for game shows add some barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Amazon supported Volley through ISP tooling and later invested via the Alexa Fund in the 2024 Series C rather than copying it.

market_need_then: Smart speaker adoption was surging in 2017 and 2018. By March 2018 Volley's voice catalog had over half a million monthly users, and Amazon reported Volley as a top earner in the Alexa developer rewards program.

branding.domain_note: Used volleygames.com as the main domain, then weekend.com after the 2026 rename. How the weekend.com domain was obtained is not stated.

identity.visual_style: Playful family game night look per the Weekend site
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful, warm and social; headlines such as 'Game night, every night'

rebrands.why: No company explanation found; commentary ties it to the move to TV and a family and friends framing

brand_strength.rationale: Volley was known inside the Alexa ecosystem as top-ranked voice games, but I found no press about the brand itself. Licensed brands such as Jeopardy and Wheel of Fortune carry more recognition than the company name.

pivots.to: Voice games across speakers, TV and mobile, with acquisitions of Voxion and Matchbox
pivots.why: Expanding platforms and content; stated in company press and podcasts

pivots.to: Weekend, AI games and entertainment for TV
pivots.why: Company now centers on TV; formal reason not found

outcome_analysis: Volley rode the 2017 and 2018 smart speaker boom with hit Alexa games, reaching more than half a million monthly users within a year of launch. It then raised Lightspeed led rounds in 2020 and 2022 and a 55 million dollar Series C in July 2024, and renamed itself Weekend in February 2026 as it focused on TV. The company is active with about 80 staff.
notes: Series A and B dates conflict: Lightspeed says Series A 2020 and Series B 2022. Aggregators claim a 14 million Series A in May 2018, a 37 million Series B in December 2021 and totals from 65.8 to 115 million; all unverified and not recorded as rounds. The YC page says founded 2016. No outcome event found because the company is active. Founder education and prior employers not found.
